name: Zurich
tagline: Switzerland's biggest city, a lake-and-river old town of church spires, guild houses, chocolate shops and swimming spots, with the Alps on the horizon.
highlight: The Limmat river with the twin towers of the Grossmünster and old-town rooftops from Lindenhof hill.
shortDescription: A compact, clean city on Lake Zurich, with a medieval old town, Bahnhofstrasse shopping, museums, river swimming and easy day trips to the mountains.
metaDescription: A Zurich travel guide: the old town and Grossmünster, Lindenhof, Lake Zurich, Bahnhofstrasse, Kunsthaus, food, where to stay, how to get around and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Old town, lake, banking, museums, chocolate
goodFor: City breaks, arrival and departure, culture, shopping, day trips

image.alt: Zurich's old town, the Limmat river and the twin towers of the Grossmünster

intro: Zurich is Switzerland's largest city and financial centre, home to about 440,000 people, and the country's main gateway, with an airport connected to the centre by a 10-minute train. It sits at the northern end of Lake Zurich, split by the Limmat river, and its old town of cobbled lanes, guild halls and church spires is compact enough to walk in an afternoon.

The city is cleaner, greener and more relaxed than its banking reputation suggests. In summer, locals swim in the lake and float down the river, and open-air bathhouses turn into evening bars. Museums include the Kunsthaus, one of Switzerland's best art museums, the Swiss National Museum and a lively design scene in Zurich West. Bahnhofstrasse is one of the world's most expensive shopping streets.

Zurich works best as a two-day stop at the start or end of a trip. It is also a good base for day trips, since Lucerne is 45 minutes away, and Rhine Falls, Winterthur and the mountains of central Switzerland are within an hour or two.

whyVisit.intro: Zurich is an easy, polished city that mixes history, water and culture.

attractionsIntro: Most sights cluster around the Limmat and the lake.

attractions.name: The Old Town and Grossmünster

image.file: File:Zürich mit Altstadt, Limmat und Grossmünster.jpg
image.alt: The Grossmünster's twin towers above the Limmat river in Zurich

attractions.text: A Romanesque church with twin towers, where the Reformation in Zurich began under Huldrych Zwingli, with a climbable tower and views over the old town.
attractions.tip: Climb the tower in the morning.

attractions.name: Lindenhof

image.alt: The Lindenhof hill square above the old town of Zurich

attractions.text: A tree-shaded square on a hill above the Limmat, on the site of a Roman fort, with a chess board and views.

attractions.name: Lake Zurich and Bürkliplatz

image.alt: Bürkliplatz and the Quaibrücke bridge seen from Lake Zurich

attractions.text: The lakefront promenade, boats and swimming spots, with the Alps visible on clear days.

attractions.name: Bahnhofstrasse

attractions.text: A tree-lined shopping street from the station to the lake, with chocolate shops, watchmakers and banks.

attractions.name: Fraumünster and Chagall windows
attractions.text: A church with stained glass windows by Marc Chagall.

attractions.name: Kunsthaus Zürich
attractions.text: One of Switzerland's leading art museums, with Impressionists and Giacometti.

thingsToDoIntro: Zurich rewards a slow pace and a swim.

thingsToDo.title: Swim in the Limmat or the lake
thingsToDo.text: Public bathhouses and free swimming spots.
thingsToDo.tip: Go on hot days, from June.

thingsToDo.title: Go up Uetliberg
thingsToDo.text: A local mountain with city views, reached by train.

Links to Munich, Milan, Paris and Vienna.

faq.a: Two days. A third allows a day trip.
Yes, among the most expensive cities in the world.
